facts.text: Fallen Astronaut Memorial was deployed at Hadley Rille during Apollo 15 in 1971.
A small aluminium sculpture by Paul Van Hoeydonck, placed by Scott alongside a plaque listing 14 astronauts and cosmonauts who had died. The only artwork on another world.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
While not a science instrument, it represents the first deliberate act of artistic and memorial expression on another celestial body, raising important questions about heritage preservation in space.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Hadley Rille.
The only known artwork on another world; a replica is in the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum. Its existence sparked discussion about the ethics of art and commerce in space.
